details: U.S. Initial Jobless Claims for the week ending April 20, 2026, rose to 214,000, exceeding the anticipated 211,000. This increase suggests a potential weakening in the U.S. labor market, which could lead the Federal Reserve to consider earlier interest rate cuts. While lower interest rates typically enhance liquidity for risk assets like Bitcoin, the cryptocurrency remained stable around $77,700, potentially having already factored in such expectations. Altcoins, however, experienced some selling pressure, partly influenced by a Toncoin unlock event.
title: US Jobless Claims Rise, Signaling Potential Fed Rate Cuts; Bitcoin Stable

details: Bitcoin saw a 4.3% increase in the last 24 hours, reaching $78,794.56 by April 22, 2026, 8:00 p.m. UTC. This rally is underpinned by strong inflows into Bitcoin spot Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs), which recorded their sixth consecutive day of positive net inflows, attracting over a quarter-billion dollars this week. Analysts attribute this positive movement to renewed market liquidity, increased corporate Bitcoin purchases, and a broader risk-on sentiment observed in equity markets. Ethereum also experienced a notable gain of 3.4%.
title: Bitcoin Rallies Amid Sixth Consecutive Day of ETF Inflows

details: Global retail cryptocurrency activity experienced its second consecutive quarterly decline in Q1 2026. The total attributed volume dropped 11% year-over-year to $979 billion. This downturn is largely driven by macroeconomic factors, including a global risk-off sentiment, uncertainties surrounding U.S. tariff policy, a strengthening dollar, and elevated real yields. These conditions have historically suppressed retail participation in crypto markets. Bitcoin itself saw a 22% decline over the quarter, highlighting its sensitivity to broader macro conditions.
title: Global Retail Crypto Volume Down 11% in Q1 2026 Amid Risk-Off Environment
